chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Quran was revealed with the meaning of 'Iyyaka' (You) referring to the general community, while 'Yā Jārat' (O Neighbor) was heard by the specific neighbor.

And in another report, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: Its meaning is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, reproached His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) with, so He means by it what has passed in the Quran, such as His saying: 'And if We had not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little,' meaning by that others than him.

key_terms.إِيَّاكَ: You (singular, emphatic pronoun used in Quranic address)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Iyyaka' in the Quran and does it refer only to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the grammatical principle of 'Iyyaka' (You) in Surah Al-Fatiha, asserting that the address is directed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as the primary representative, yet encompasses the entire Ummah. The second narration reinforces this by citing the verse 'And if We had not strengthened you...' (Al-Isra: 74), demonstrating that divine address to the Prophet often implies a meaning that extends to the general believers, a concept central to Shia exegetical tradition regarding the relationship between the Imam/Prophet and the community.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Quran was Revealed Meaning you (as the second person) and Making the neighbours (third person) hear it’.

And in another report, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Its Meaning what Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Reproached with upon Hisazwj Prophetas, so its Meaning is what has continued in the Quran, for example Hisazwj Words [17:74] And had We not Affirmed you, you would have almost inclined towards them a little, Meaning by that others than himsaww’. (i.e., the word ‘you’ is not addressed to Rasool-Allahsaww, but to the general Muslims).
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Holy Quran was revealed in a manner like, ‘I speak to you, but it is the neighbor who must listen.’”

It is narrated, in another Hadith, from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The meaning of ‘I speak to you, but it is the neighbor who must listen’, is that whenever Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has addressed His prophet in critical expressions they, in fact, are addressed to others and not the Holy Prophet such as: ‘Had We not strengthened your faith you might have relied on them some how,’ [17:74] is addressed to others (not the Holy Prophet).”’
